blindSummary:
This territory operates outside the country's federal legal framework in practice. In February 2017, local law-enforcement and security officials launched an anti-gay purge, rounding up dozens of men, holding them in unofficial detention facilities (documented by name and location, including a secret prison in a satellite town), humiliating, starving and torturing them, forcibly disappearing some, and returning others to families "barely alive from beatings" after captors exposed them and encouraged relatives to carry out honour killings. An independent national newspaper reported in January 2019 that persecution had resumed and the satellite-town facility was "full again", while the regional leader's press chief publicly denied that any unofficial detention sites exist.

The pattern has mutated and continues: a regional rights-monitoring group documented at least seven cases of local security forces blackmailing detained homosexual men into "volunteering" for front-line conscription in the country's external war (one already killed), and a prominent human-rights documentation society found a mass wave of unlawful detentions tied to forced conscription. In 2021 the regional leader's aide announced the abduction of two men who had been evacuated abroad, taken at a district police station. A foreign home ministry's June 2025 country-of-origin note for asylum claims expressly treats this border zone — and trans people generally — as likely to face treatment amounting to persecution, an exception to its finding of no state-persecution risk elsewhere in the country; it documents systematic campaigns between 2017 and 2024 including abductions, torture and extrajudicial killings, and notes that detention violence spread beyond this zone after the 2023 "extremist" designation.

For a visitor discovered or outed, the documented record is detention without legal process, torture, coerced conscription or death, with no functioning judicial remedy. The scale of extrajudicial killing and secret-prison infrastructure documented here has no confirmed equivalent anywhere else in the country.
